c_ssrs.name: Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS)
c_ssrs.purpose: Assess suicidal ideation intensity and suicidal behavior. Medico-legal documentation standard.

questions.question: Have you wished you were dead or wished you could go to sleep and not wake up?
Have you actually had any thoughts of killing yourself?
Have you been thinking about how you might do this?
Have you had these thoughts and had some intention of acting on them?
Have you started to work out or worked out the details of how to kill yourself? Do you intend to carry out this plan?

passive.description: Passive death wish only — no active plan or intent
passive.action: Monitor at next session; document verbatim denial of active SI

active_without_plan.description: Active SI, no specific method or plan
active_without_plan.action: Safety planning required; assess means access; increase visit frequency

active_with_plan.description: Active SI with specific method but no stated intent
active_with_plan.action: Safety planning mandatory; means restriction counseling; consider crisis consultation

active_with_intent.description: Active SI with plan AND intent to act
active_with_intent.action: EMERGENT: Psychiatric evaluation for inpatient hospitalization; do not leave patient alone; contact emergency services if needed

required_documentation: Presence or absence of suicidal ideation (both must be documented every session)
Presence or absence of homicidal ideation
Next follow-up date with contingency plan
c_ssrs.legal_note: Failure to document negative findings (patient denied SI) is a major medico-legal liability. Document denial explicitly even when all screens are negative.

phq9.name: Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9)
phq9.purpose: Screen and monitor depression severity. Validated for MDD diagnosis and treatment response tracking.
phq9.instructions: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?

questions.question: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Poor appetite or overeating
Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed? Or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way

phq9.item_9_protocol: Any score ≥1 on item 9 requires immediate C-SSRS administration and safety planning documentation.

gad7.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-item (GAD-7)
gad7.purpose: Screen and monitor generalized anxiety disorder severity.
gad7.instructions: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?

questions.question: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Trouble relaxing
Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
Becoming easily annoyed or irritable
Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen

severe.action: Active pharmacological + psychological treatment; assess for panic disorder comorbidity

pcl5.name: PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5)
pcl5.purpose: Screen for PTSD and monitor treatment response. Maps directly to DSM-5 PTSD criteria.
pcl5.instructions: In the past month, how much were you bothered by the following problems?

questions.question: Repeated, disturbing, and unwanted memories of the stressful experience
Repeated, disturbing dreams of the stressful experience
Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
Feeling very upset when something reminded you of the stressful experience
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
Avoiding memories, thoughts, or feelings related to the stressful experience
Avoiding external reminders of the stressful experience
Trouble remembering important parts of the stressful experience
Having strong negative beliefs about yourself, other people, or the world
Blaming yourself or someone else for the stressful experience or what happened after it
Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame
Loss of interest in activities that you used to enjoy
Feeling distant or cut off from other people
Trouble experiencing positive feelings
Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively
Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
Being 'superalert' or watchful or on guard
Feeling jumpy or easily startled
Having difficulty concentrating
Trouble falling or staying asleep

probable_ptsd.action: Full PTSD assessment; initiate trauma-focused therapy (PE/CPT/EMDR); consider sertraline or paroxetine

pcl5.scoring_note: Provisional PTSD diagnosis if ≥1 item in B cluster, ≥1 in C, ≥2 in D, ≥2 in E each score ≥2.
